events.content:
I want a small app for keeping track of the books I'm reading.

When I open it I want to see what I'm currently reading and what I've finished. I want to add a book from a form, mark one as finished, and click through to a book to see its title, author and my notes. I'd like to be able to send someone a link to a single book.

Nothing fancy and no accounts. Skip the database, save the books to a JSON file so they're still there after a restart.
I'll check what's in the workspace first so the app fits whatever is already there.

events.content:
I've built the books app. Start it with npm start and open http://localhost:3000. The page shows what you're currently reading and what you've finished, with a form to add a book underneath.

- Adding a book: you give a title, an author and optional notes. The title and author are required.
- Finishing a book: each book you're reading has a "Mark finished" button, both on the main page and on the book's own page. Finished books show the date you finished them, newest first.
- Book page: each book has its own page at /books/<id> with the title, author, your notes, and a link you can copy and send to someone.
- Saving: books are saved to data/books.json and are still there after a restart. You can use a different file by setting DATA_FILE, and a different port with PORT. I added data/ to .gitignore so your reading list doesn't get committed.

It uses Node's built-in web server with no extra packages. The code is in server.js, src/store.js (saving and loading) and src/app.js (pages and form handling).

npm test runs 7 tests and they all pass. They cover adding, finishing, notes display, missing fields, unknown books, share links and restarts. I also added a book on the real server and confirmed it was written to the JSON file.

Two things to know about sharing links:
- Reaching the app: as it stands the app only runs on your own computer, so a link you send won't open for anyone else. They can only open it if the app is running somewhere they can reach, like your home network or a small hosting service.
- No accounts: anyone who can open a book's page can also add books or mark them finished. That's fine for a personal app, but it matters if you put it online.

Editing and deleting books aren't included yet, since you didn't ask for them.
